name: Golden Door Scholars — Scholarship for DACA & Undocumented Students
description: Golden Door Scholars provides full-tuition scholarships covering tuition, room, and board for undocumented and DACA-recipient students to pursue four-year bachelor's degrees at partner colleges across the United States. Since 2013 the program has supported hundreds of students who lack lawful immigration status but demonstrate strong academic achievement (minimum 3.2 unweighted GPA) and high financial need. Beyond funding, scholars receive career readiness programming, mentorship from professionals and alumni, and a supportive community network. Applicants must have graduated from a U.S. high school and lived in the United States for at least four years. The scholarship is renewable for up to four years of undergraduate study.
eligibility: Undocumented, DACA, or TPS students who graduated from a U.S. high school; minimum 3.2 unweighted GPA; demonstrated high financial need; must have lived in the U.S. for at least 4 years prior to application
amount: Full tuition, room, and board at partner colleges (4-year award)
applicationProcess: Submit an online application through the Golden Door Scholars website. The application requires a 500-word essay, a 2-minute video, and unofficial high school transcripts. Applications typically open in the fall for the following academic year. Scholarship recipients are matched with a regional partner college.
geographicScope: United States — partner colleges in select states
documentsRequired: Unofficial high school transcripts, 500-word essay, 2-minute video, proof of immigration status (DACA, TPS, or affidavit of undocumented status), proof of U.S. residency for at least 4 years

name: Refugee Career Pathways (RCP) Program
description: The Refugee Career Pathways program, administered by the U.S. Office of Refugee Resettlement within the Administration for Children and Families, helps refugees and other ORR-eligible populations achieve economic self-sufficiency through professional certification, credential evaluation, and job training. Established in 2018, RCP connects participants with education and training aligned to their prior professional experience and career goals. The program covers costs for credentialing exams, licensing fees, vocational courses, and in some cases provides direct financial assistance for childcare and transportation while participants complete career development activities. RCP operates through a network of community-based organizations and resettlement agencies across multiple states.
eligibility: Refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, Special Immigrant Visa holders, and other populations eligible for ORR services; must be within the ORR eligibility window (typically 5 years from arrival); no citizenship or permanent residency required
amount: Varies — covers credentialing exams, licensing fees, vocational training costs, and may include childcare/transportation stipends
applicationProcess: Contact a local ORR-funded resettlement agency or community-based organization that participates in the RCP program. A career navigator or case manager will assess your skills, prior education, and career goals, then develop a personalized career plan. Training and credentialing are arranged through partnering educational institutions and certification bodies.
geographicScope: United States — multiple states through ORR-funded partner organizations
documentsRequired: Proof of ORR-eligible immigration status, prior education and work experience documentation (if available), identification documents, intake assessment with case manager

name: New York Professional Pathways for High-Skilled Immigrants
organization: New York State Department of Labor
description: The New York State Professional Pathways for High-Skilled Immigrants Program provides state-funded grants to community-based organizations that help skilled immigrants and refugees find employment matching their professional qualifications and experience. With $4.38 million in total funding, the program supports credential evaluation, professional licensing assistance, skills-bridge training, English language instruction for professional contexts, and direct job placement services. The program specifically targets immigrants who hold professional degrees or significant work experience from their home countries but face barriers to re-entering their fields in the United States due to licensing requirements, language gaps, or lack of U.S. work experience.
eligibility: High-skilled immigrants and refugees residing in New York State who hold professional degrees or significant work experience from their countries of origin; must be authorized to work in the United States; no specific visa type restriction
amount: Free services funded through $4.38 million in state grants to provider organizations
applicationProcess: Contact one of the state-funded community-based provider organizations in New York. Providers conduct an intake assessment of your professional background, credentials, and career goals. Services include credential evaluation, professional licensing guidance, skills-bridge training, job readiness workshops, and direct employer connections.
documentsRequired: Proof of New York State residency, work authorization documentation, professional credentials and academic transcripts from home country, resume or CV, identification documents

name: Achievement Scholarship for Refugees and Immigrants of Wake County
organization: College Board / Wake County community organizations
description: The Achievement Scholarship for Refugees and Immigrants of Wake County provides financial support to graduating high school seniors who are refugees or immigrants residing in Wake County, North Carolina. The scholarship helps recipients pursue professional certifications, associate degrees, or bachelor's degrees at institutions within North Carolina. It recognizes academic achievement, community involvement, and the unique challenges faced by students navigating the U.S. education system while adapting to a new country. The scholarship aims to close the opportunity gap for first-generation immigrant and refugee students in the Wake County area who demonstrate both academic promise and financial need.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors who are refugees or immigrants residing in Wake County, North Carolina; must plan to pursue a professional certification, associate, or bachelor's degree at a North Carolina institution
applicationProcess: Apply through the College Board BigFuture scholarship search platform or through the Wake County scholarship portal. The application typically requires academic transcripts, a personal essay describing your immigration journey and educational goals, a letter of recommendation, and proof of Wake County residency.
geographicScope: Wake County, North Carolina — for study at any North Carolina institution
documentsRequired: High school transcripts, personal essay, letter of recommendation, proof of Wake County residency, proof of refugee or immigrant status

name: Employment Skills Training (EST) for Newcomers — Canada
description: The Employment Skills Training (EST) program, offered through the Immigrant Education Society in Canada, provides free vocational and job-readiness training for landed immigrants and refugees. The program covers essential workplace skills including Canadian workplace culture, resume writing and interview preparation, computer skills, industry-specific certifications, and job search strategies. EST is designed for newcomers who need practical skills to enter the Canadian labor market and includes hands-on training in sectors with high demand for workers such as healthcare support, food services, retail, and administrative roles. The program also provides referrals to additional settlement services including language training, housing assistance, and credential recognition.
eligibility: Landed immigrants (permanent residents) and refugees in Canada; must be eligible to work in Canada; all skill levels welcome; priority given to newcomers within their first 5 years of arrival
applicationProcess: Contact the Immigrant Education Society directly by phone, email, or in person at their Calgary location. Complete an intake assessment to determine eligibility and skill level. Participants are enrolled in training modules based on their career interests and current skills. Training schedules are flexible with both full-time and part-time options available.
geographicScope: Alberta, Canada — primarily Calgary-based with some online components
documentsRequired: Proof of permanent residency or refugee status in Canada, government-issued photo ID, social insurance number (SIN), language assessment results (if available)
